items.title: FPL GW8 Team Selection: My Saka & Szoboszlai Replacements! 🤕 | Transfers & Captain
items.headline: Saka injury drives Raya and Mbeumo move for Gameweek 8
items.summary:
Gameweek 8 is dominated by injuries, with Bukayo Saka expected to miss at least the weekend and potentially several matches with a quad or hip-flexor issue. Despite his 50% availability flag in FPL, the assessment is that his chance of playing is under 1%, following Mikel Arteta’s pessimistic comments. Saka is therefore sold rather than benched, while Soasai is also ruled out for one to three matches and is no longer an appealing long-term squad hold. Four saved free transfers provide flexibility after a poor Gameweek 7, in which the team’s rank falls from 25,000 to 131,000 across two rounds.

The preferred immediate double move is Saka and Tottenham goalkeeper Kinsky out for Brentford goalkeeper Raya and Manchester United midfielder Bryan Mbeumo. Raya completes a triple Arsenal defensive unit alongside Calafiori and Conor, with Arsenal carrying the standout 48% clean-sheet probability in Gameweek 8. Kinsky has Chelsea away, one of the worst clean-sheet fixtures of the round, while Spurs continue to concede despite respectable defensive underlying numbers. Calafiori and Conor are backed to start against Everton, while Mahranovic and Thomas remain playable because their defensive-contribution floors and set-piece or shooting upside offer the prospect of major hauls rather than repeated one- or two-point returns.

Mbeumo is preferred to Morgan Gibbs-White as the Saka replacement despite Manchester United’s poor form. Mbeumo dominates United’s attacking output, records roughly 4.0 xG and nearly 1.0 xA in seven matches, has eight big chances, and ranks among the Premier League’s strongest players for non-penalty expected goal involvement per start. His upcoming opponents — Bournemouth, Chelsea and Aston Villa in particular — play high lines that suit his pace and counter-attacking profile. He also has some set pieces, potential penalties if Bruno is absent, and could benefit from a managerial change. Gibbs-White offers penalties, corners and bonus potential, but Nottingham Forest have scored only five times, won once, and post weaker attacking projections and underlying numbers.

Erling Haaland is the captaincy choice after being declared fully fit and rested in midweek, with Manchester City projected for 2.08 goals. Chelsea are almost level at 2.07 projected goals, supporting Cole Palmer, Rogers and Joao Pedro, while Pascal Gross starts against Liverpool because Brighton are in form and Gross has penalties and set pieces. Maxim Diper stays benched against Liverpool: his recent returns rely heavily on clean sheets plus occasional attacking returns, but his underlying attacking numbers are modest and the fixture sharply reduces both routes to points. Rather than spend another transfer on Soasai’s replacement, the plan is to hold, use Diper as cover if needed, and target Manzambi or Creepy Jr. from Gameweek 9, when their fitness and fixtures improve.
key_points: Sell Bukayo Saka in Gameweek 8, as his quad or hip-flexor injury is expected to keep him out for at least this weekend and likely longer.
The preferred two-transfer move is Kinsky and Saka to Raya and Bryan Mbeumo, completing a triple Arsenal defence.
Captain Haaland after his fitness clearance, with Manchester City carrying the highest Gameweek 8 goal projection at 2.08.
Start Palmer, Rogers, Joao Pedro and Gross, with Chelsea projected for 2.07 goals and Gross retaining set-piece and penalty routes to returns.
Bench Maxim Diper against Liverpool because his low attacking volume and reduced clean-sheet odds make his recent returns difficult to sustain.
Do not rush a Soasai replacement despite his one-to-three-match absence; preserve transfers and reassess Manzambi or Creepy Jr. for Gameweek 9.
Mbeumo is favoured over Gibbs-White because of his elite shot and big-chance volume, strong share of Manchester United’s attack and fixtures suited to counter-attacking football.
Arsenal are the leading clean-sheet bet for Gameweek 8 at 48%, while Kinsky at Chelsea is among the weakest defensive options.

items.headline: Saka Injury Pushes Manzambi and Tavernier to the Top of Gameweek 7 Midfield Plans
items.summary:
Bukayo Saka’s injury is the central Gameweek 7 problem, with a move to Aston Villa’s Manzambi emerging as the preferred replacement for managers seeking upside. Bournemouth’s Marcus Tavernier is also a leading target, particularly for those selling Dominik Szoboszlai, while Declan Rice is viewed as Arsenal’s safest attacking alternative: he offers set pieces, defensive-contribution points and steady returns, even if he lacks the explosive ceiling of more advanced midfielders. Martin Odegaard, Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke are less convincing Arsenal replacements because of role uncertainty and reduced attacking balance without Saka and the other regular wide options.

Bryan Mbeumo and Morgan Gibbs-White divide opinion. Mbeumo is backed as the stronger of the pair because he is playing up front for Manchester United and remains their likeliest route to attacking returns against Bournemouth, despite concerns over the club’s poor form and internal tension. Gibbs-White has penalties and a favourable Ipswich fixture, but Nottingham Forest’s performances under Oliver Glasner are unconvincing and the schedule soon turns difficult, with Brentford, Manchester City, Bournemouth and Chelsea among the upcoming opponents. Both are acceptable short-term picks, but neither is an ideal long-term transfer compared with Tavernier or Manzambi.

Cole Palmer is a logical straight swap for Saka on price, but bringing him in alongside Joao Pedro and Morgan Rogers creates an uncomfortable Chelsea triple-up. That concentration raises the risk that one poor Chelsea performance damages the entire gameweek, although Palmer’s penalty duties make him an attractive captain candidate against Spurs. Joao Pedro is the alternative Chelsea captain and is preferred by some because of his recent form, but Palmer’s midfielder scoring, clean-sheet point and penalties provide a higher safety net. Erling Haaland remains the exceptional premium forward, while Palmer is the more appealing midfield captaincy route.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin is strongly preferred to Nicolas Jackson and Dominic Solanke as a forward transfer. He is on penalties, acts as his side’s focal point and offers better value than pricier alternatives, even if his high ownership makes him less exciting. Managers with Josh King or Gonzalo should give them one final chance against Coventry rather than sell immediately: Fulham’s attack continues to create opportunities, and both forwards have favourable fixtures against promoted opposition. The exception is Yoane Wissa, who can be sold for Calvert-Lewin. A bench boost featuring Hall, Thomas and Gross is also endorsed, as the bench is unlikely to look materially stronger later.
key_points: Sell injured Bukayo Saka for Manzambi or Tavernier if chasing attacking upside; Declan Rice is the safer Arsenal replacement.
Bryan Mbeumo is preferred to Morgan Gibbs-White, with his centre-forward role making him Manchester United’s most appealing attacker against Bournemouth.
Avoid overcommitting to three Chelsea attackers unless comfortable with the volatility; Palmer is a viable Saka replacement but adds concentration risk alongside Joao Pedro and Rogers.
Captain Palmer over Joao Pedro if choosing Chelsea coverage, largely because Palmer is on penalties and benefits from midfielder scoring.
Calvert-Lewin is the leading forward buy ahead of Jackson and Solanke due to penalties, role and value.
Hold Josh King and Gonzalo for the Coventry fixture, but Wissa is a sellable route to Calvert-Lewin.
Start Tavernier and Schade over Solanke; Solanke’s Chelsea fixture makes him the bench candidate.

items.headline: Mbeumo edges Gibbs-White as Saliba uncertainty shapes Gameweek 8 plans
items.summary:
An 80-point Gameweek 7 lifts the squad inside the top 50,000, with Arsenal’s home meeting with Everton underpinning the Gameweek 8 selection. David Raya and William Saliba are retained alongside Konsa, creating a heavy defensive commitment to the Everton fixture. Saliba’s recent start raises some concern over his fitness and minutes, but his quality makes him difficult to bench.

The main starting-XI dilemma is Lewis Hall versus Di Kyper. Hall has the stronger fixture, but Di Kyper’s high ownership and advanced left-wing role give him a compelling floor and upside. The decision remains open, with Di Kyper potentially moving into the side despite the fixture disadvantage. Pascal Gross is also considered playable even away to Liverpool, while Sangare is expected to start but remains a riskier option unlikely to make the final XI.

Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers are firm holds. Tottenham at home is not viewed as a fixture severe enough to force a sale, and there is no obvious replacement worth a transfer. If Saliba’s red flag persists, the preferred move is a sale for Bryan Mbeumo or Morgan Gibbs-White. Gibbs-White offers penalties and the benefit of no European commitments, but Mbeumo currently leads the race because he is operating at centre-forward and carries strong goal threat, even within an underperforming Manchester United side.

The forward line needs no intervention: João Pedro, Erling Haaland and Dominic Calvert-Lewin are all backed for Gameweek 8 and beyond. Haaland is the current captain, though Palmer is an appealing differential captaincy alternative for managers willing to oppose the popular choice.
key_points: Arsenal’s home fixture against Everton drives a defensive triple-up centred on Raya and Saliba, with Konsa also starting.
Saliba is difficult to bench despite fitness and minutes concerns, but a continued red flag could prompt a transfer out.

items.headline: João Pedro edges Haaland for the captaincy in Gameweek 8 wildcard draft
items.summary:
A Gameweek 8 wildcard draft is built around Morgan Rogers, Cole Palmer and João Pedro, with João Pedro preferred as captain at home to Spurs and Erling Haaland handed the vice-captaincy. The forward line otherwise follows the popular structure: Haaland and João Pedro are joined by a flexible third striker slot, with Dominic Calvert-Lewin the preferred pick but Kostas, Nicolas Jackson or Barry viable alternatives depending on budget and preference.

David Raya starts in goal alongside a £4.0m reserve, while Arsenal’s defence is doubled up with Riccardo Calafiori. Calafiori is favoured over the cheaper Ezri Konsa because of his stronger attacking potential and better long-term route into the Arsenal side, particularly with William Saliba expected to return. The remaining defence uses Mepham and Decordova as starters, with Van Hecke and Bobby Thomas on the bench. Managers with extra squad value can retain Konsa and field a triple-Arsenal defence instead of starting Decordova in Gameweek 8.

In midfield, Jérémy Doku is the main calculated punt, with Semenyo expected to be unavailable for the next couple of months and Doku seen as the likeliest beneficiary. Palmer and Rogers are locked into the wildcard midfield, while Pascal Groß starts despite an away fixture at Liverpool. Man Zaha is benched because he is a slight fitness doubt, but remains a strong target from Gameweek 9 onwards, so there is little concern if he misses the immediate round.
key_points: Captain João Pedro at home to Spurs in Gameweek 8, with Haaland as vice-captain.

items.title: My FPL GW8 TEAM SELECTION! 🔥 SAKA OUT ❌
items.headline: Saka injury forces move as Gibbs-White leads the replacement shortlist
items.summary:
A 70-point Gameweek brings a small green arrow, driven by Raya and Konsa’s nine-point returns, another Groß contribution and Erling Haaland’s captaincy brace. The recent transfers have made little immediate impact: Wissa and Solanke left for Rogers and Barry, while King has blanked twice despite strong underlying numbers. The squad’s main new problem is Bukayo Saka, who suffers a quad issue against Bayern and looks set for a spell out after Mikel Arteta says the medical staff are concerned.

The preferred Gameweek 8 XI is Raya; Konsa, Schär and De Cuyper; Saka, Cole Palmer, Rogers, King and Groß; João Pedro and Haaland. De Cuyper starts despite Liverpool away because of his advanced left-wing role and 2.6 expected goal involvements, while Groß is trusted for his set pieces, penalties and Brighton’s attacking form. Schär is a defensive concern given Newcastle’s poor clean-sheet record, though Lewis Hall would be more playable for his attacking threat. Van Hecke is benched for Chelsea away, with Barry and the doubtful Mendy also among the substitutes.

Haaland is the captain at home to Aston Villa after Manchester City confirm he is fully available following a Champions League rest; Palmer is vice-captain for Chelsea’s home match against Tottenham. Arsenal have the highest projected goal total of the week at 2.2, with Chelsea and City next on 2.1, but Saka’s likely absence makes his sale unavoidable. Palmer remains a hold, while King gets one final chance against Liverpool despite his frustrating lack of returns and 2.8 xGI.

With two free transfers and £0.2m in the bank, the leading plan is Saka to Morgan Gibbs-White and Trevoh Chalobah to Mohamedovic, leaving £1.8m for later upgrades. Gibbs-White is narrowly preferred to En-Nesyri because of Ipswich away, penalties, free-kicks and corners, although En-Nesyri has stronger underlying data and should lead Manchester United’s line while Sesko is injured. Other routes include Saka to Mbeumo, Ødegaard or Shawda, potentially combined with Chalobah to Gabriel or Calafiori, but the Gabriel route can restrict future access to midfield targets. A hit to add Crooks alongside Gibbs-White and Gabriel is considered but rejected, particularly with King facing a promising fixture. If Rogers is not already owned, he ranks above Gibbs-White and En-Nesyri as the Saka replacement.
key_points: Sell Bukayo Saka unless an unexpected fitness update clears his quad injury; the early signs suggest a meaningful absence.
Captain Erling Haaland against Aston Villa after Manchester City confirm he is 100% available; Cole Palmer is vice-captain against Tottenham.

items.headline: Mbeumo edges Gibbs-White as Szoboszlai exit unlocks Gameweek 8 move
items.summary:
The squad enters Gameweek 8 on the back of an 80-point haul that lifts overall rank from 75,000 to 40,000. The previous week’s transfers, Jamie Vardy to Van Hecke and Yoane Wissa to Dominic Calvert-Lewin, produce 13 points between them, while the Arsenal defensive trio of David Raya, Riccardo Calafiori and Konsa delivers the decisive returns. With three free transfers and £1.9m in the bank, the priority is now to preserve a strong structure rather than make unnecessary defensive changes.

Raya, Calafiori and Konsa are set to start against Everton, although Calafiori carries a minor rotation concern after playing Bayern Munich in midweek. Lewis Hall is currently preferred over De Cuyper for the final defensive spot because Newcastle face a weaker opponent in Crystal Palace, but De Cuyper’s advanced wing role for Brighton and high ownership make that a close call despite Liverpool being the opposition. No defender transfer is planned before the international break unless an injury intervenes, with Vuskovic, Silva and Muraremovic among potential later targets.

Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Pascal Gross are retained in midfield. Gross has a difficult trip to Liverpool, while Sangares should start because of suspensions, but Gross’s reliable minutes, set pieces, penalties and huge ownership make him the safer selection. The main transfer is Dominik Szoboszlai out, with Bryan Mbeumo narrowly favoured over Morgan Gibbs-White. Gibbs-White offers penalties, guaranteed 90-minute appearances and Ipswich away immediately, but Mbeumo has stronger goal threat, costs £0.1m less and is currently essential to Manchester United’s attack amid injuries elsewhere. The risk is that a potential managerial change could alter Mbeumo’s role or minutes; Gibbs-White remains a viable alternative, particularly for his longer-term schedule.

Up front, Erling Haaland, Joao Pedro and Calvert-Lewin are viewed as long-term holds because all are nailed and two take penalties. Haaland keeps the captaincy for Aston Villa away, although Palmer at home to Spurs is tempting as a penalty-taking midfielder. Palmer’s recent underlying numbers are not convincing enough to dislodge Haaland yet. Bukayo Saka’s quad injury is expected to rule him out until after the international break, so owners should prepare to sell. Martin Odegaard is the Arsenal midfielder most likely to benefit through stronger minutes and a possible share of penalties, but Mbeumo, Gibbs-White and Rogers are preferred replacement routes; Saka funds can also upgrade a goalkeeper to Raya or strengthen Arsenal defence.
key_points: The likely transfer is Szoboszlai to Mbeumo, while Gibbs-White remains an extremely close alternative because he has Ipswich away and penalties.
Haaland is the current Gameweek 8 captain against Aston Villa, with Palmer the only serious alternative for Spurs at home.
Calafiori is started against Everton despite a rotation concern following his Champions League minutes against Bayern Munich.
Lewis Hall currently starts ahead of De Cuyper, although De Cuyper’s wing role and high ownership could yet change that bench decision.
Gross is preferred to Sangare despite Liverpool away, owing to his set pieces, penalties, secure minutes and high effective ownership.

items.title: FPL GW8 EXPERT Transfer Trends & Best Captain! 🧠 100 Experts Reveal Gameweek 8 Team Plans
items.headline: Haaland remains the Gameweek 8 captain, but experts pivot towards Leeds and away from Newcastle
items.summary:
Gameweek 8 is largely a week to hold: 56% of the 100 FPL experts make no transfer, 27% make one and 16% make two, with only one Wildcard and one Bench Boost in use. The prevailing strategy is to bank transfers where possible, with managers able to accumulate up to five free moves. Chips are not a priority, although 83% of experts still retain their Free Hit.

Where experts do act, they are moving away from injured assets and several Newcastle players. Dominik Szoboszlai is the clearest sale, with all 14 expert owners transferring him out. Barry, Lewis Hall, Malacia and Wissa also attract notable sales, while Semedo is an obvious exit because of his long-term injury. Kinsky, Saka, Cherki and Odegaard receive smaller numbers of sales. The anti-Newcastle trend is especially clear, suggesting their assets are becoming less attractive even if an individual player has not yet become an urgent sell.

The leading replacements are Calvert-Lewin and Mohamedovic, with experts increasingly backing Leeds assets. Calvert-Lewin gains 12 new owners and approaches 50% ownership among the group, while Mohamedovic is also heavily bought. Other popular arrivals include Shaw ahead of Hull, Raya, budget defender Bobby Thomas, Tavernier, Mbeumo, João Pedro and Rodgers. The logic is fixture- and performance-based rather than chasing the previous week's points: experts are notably buying Arshavin despite wider-manager sales, while avoiding Brighton additions such as Gross, Estupiñán and Kostas because Brighton face Liverpool away and Manchester City away next.

The strongest expert-approved transfer combinations are Barry or Wissa to João Pedro or Calvert-Lewin, Malick Thiaw to Mohamedovic, and Szoboszlai to Rodgers if Rodgers is not already owned. Schär, Tavernier and Benrahma are lower-priority alternatives. Erling Haaland remains the default captain despite an away fixture at Aston Villa, backed by 57% of experts after returning to fitness. João Pedro is the main alternative at 17%, followed by Cole Palmer at 14%; Gibbs-White is a more differential option against Ipswich, provided his availability is confirmed in press conferences.
key_points: Roll a transfer if your squad is healthy: 56% of experts make no move in Gameweek 8 and chip use is almost non-existent.
Sell Szoboszlai if possible, while injured players such as Semedo and Malacia are also priority exits.
Newcastle assets are trending down, with Hall and Wissa among the notable expert sales.
Calvert-Lewin and Mohamedovic are the leading transfer targets, signalling growing expert interest in Leeds players.
Barry or Wissa to João Pedro or Calvert-Lewin rate as the most strongly supported moves among the expert data.
Avoid buying Brighton assets before difficult away fixtures against Liverpool and Manchester City.

items.title: FPL WATCHLIST GW8 WITH FPL HARRY 🔎 | FODEN, ISAK, MUHAREMOVIĆ | FPL Tips 26/27
items.headline: João Pedro edges Haaland for captaincy as Calvert-Lewin becomes the key forward transfer
items.summary:
João Pedro is the preferred captain for Gameweek 8 as Chelsea host Tottenham, with the fixture viewed as a strong opportunity for Chelsea’s attack despite Spurs ranking well on expected goals conceded since Gameweek 2. Tottenham’s defensive numbers are questioned on eye-test grounds after they allow repeated central transitions against Coventry, while Chelsea are expected to score freely at Stamford Bridge. Erling Haaland remains a perfectly viable alternative away to Aston Villa, but João Pedro offers a worthwhile differential captaincy play before Haaland’s appealing run against Brighton, Nottingham Forest and Fulham.

The central transfer decision is Gonzalo García to Dominic Calvert-Lewin. García has Coventry at home in Gameweek 8 and is worth keeping if funds allow, but Calvert-Lewin’s price is close to rising and Leeds’ forward is considered the safest cheap-striker option for the longer term. He combines secure minutes, penalties and reliable finishing, with Sunderland and Bournemouth next before a potential captaincy fixture at home to Coventry in Gameweek 12. García can be sold next week if managers have the funds, but those priced out by a Calvert-Lewin rise are justified in moving immediately.

Defensive transfers are less attractive in the short term because clean-sheet probabilities are low outside Arsenal. The best approach is to buy a defender who is wanted for several weeks rather than chase one fixture. Mephamović is the leading target thanks to Leeds’ defensive-contribution potential, set-piece threat and relative security of starts; Bobby Thomas is the cheaper alternative for managers needing funds, although he plays in a weaker defence. Bournemouth’s Antonio Silva remains watchlisted, while Manchester City defenders are avoided because of rotation and a recent tendency to concede chances.

In midfield, Pascal Groß and Morgan Rogers remain the strongest mid-price picks because both offer dependable minutes through the busy winter period. Manzambi is the preferred cheaper replacement for suspended Szoboszlai, ahead of Kevin Schade and Tavernier, provided his injury is cleared; Tavernier’s strong output is offset by concern over competition for Bournemouth minutes and reduced penalty prospects with Kluivert and Christie available. Phil Foden’s Champions League hat-trick puts him on the watchlist, but rotation with Cherki, Doku and other City attackers makes an immediate purchase too risky. Cole Palmer and Bukayo Saka are underperforming their prices, although Saka’s underlying numbers remain excellent and Palmer’s home match against Spurs carries obvious upside.

Alexander Isak is the premium-forward alternative if managers downgrade Saka or another midfielder, especially with Szoboszlai absent from Liverpool’s penalties, but his fitness record and upcoming Arsenal fixture temper the appeal. Nicolas Jackson is an interesting higher-upside option among the cheaper forwards, while Evanilson has a promising Bournemouth fixture run. Calvert-Lewin nevertheless stands out as the balanced choice over Barry, Kostulas and García, with Everton’s attack seen as less dependable than Leeds’ but the Leeds striker offering the clearer all-round FPL profile.
key_points: Captain João Pedro against Tottenham in Gameweek 8, with Haaland away at Aston Villa the safer but less distinctive alternative.
Move Gonzalo García to Dominic Calvert-Lewin now if a price rise would otherwise block the transfer; García can be held for Coventry at home if funds are available.
Target Mephamović as the long-term defensive buy because of Leeds’ set-piece threat, defensive contributions and stronger security than the other cheap Leeds defenders.
Avoid buying Manchester City defenders for Gameweek 8 due to rotation risk and recent defensive fragility, despite reasonable clean-sheet projections.
Keep Bukayo Saka for Everton and Hull if owned, while Cole Palmer is a tempting buy for Spurs at home but lacks the underlying data of Saka.
Prioritise Manzambi over Tavernier and Schade as a budget midfield replacement if he is fit; Tavernier faces growing minutes and penalty concerns.
Monitor Phil Foden after his Champions League hat-trick, but do not assume he starts against Aston Villa with City’s attacking rotation unresolved.
Consider Calvert-Lewin as a potential Gameweek 12 captain against Coventry, when premium captaincy options look limited.

items.title: TOP 10 PLAYERS TO BUY IN FPL GW8! 🔴 NEW MIDFIELDERS! #fpl  #premierleague
items.headline: Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer headline Gameweek 8 midfield buys as Leeds offer defensive value
items.summary:
Clean sheets are difficult to forecast in Gameweek 8, making defence a low-priority area unless a transfer is needed for structure or budget. Riccardo Calafiori is the straightforward premium-style move for managers who do not own him, but Leeds provide the more appealing longer-term route: Mitrovic and James Justin are the preferred options. Sunderland away is not an ideal immediate fixture, yet Leeds’ upcoming run makes one of their defenders worth targeting. Cheaper enablers such as Egan at Hull and Bobby Thomas also offer useful routes to free funds while benefiting from favourable fixtures.

In midfield, Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer stand out as the principal buys, with Palmer’s home fixture against Tottenham particularly attractive. Bryan Mbeumo is the stronger alternative for managers able to spend more: despite Manchester United’s broader struggles, he is playing up front and has scored in each of the last two matches. Bournemouth visit Old Trafford after a Thursday European away trip, adding to his appeal.

For lower-priced midfielders, Manzambi narrowly edges Tavernier as the preferred purchase, though both are viable. Rudoni is the budget fallback at £4.9m, combining recent returns, a strong long-term fixture run and penalty duties. Up front, the preferred three-forward structure is Erling Haaland, João Pedro and one additional striker. Dominic Calvert-Lewin is the value choice because Leeds’ fixtures improve, while Alexander Isak is the premium alternative. Brighton at home is not the easiest entry fixture, but Isak has begun the season well and is back to full fitness, making him a credible investment for managers not committing heavily to midfield.

items.title: START GROẞ & DE CUYER vs LIV (a) FPL GW8? 🐦 🔴 #fpl #premierleague #brighton #liverpool
items.headline: Bench Estupiñán, keep Groß: Liverpool trip offers a calculated Brighton dilemma
items.summary:
Pascal Groß and Pervis Estupiñán have been major recent FPL scorers, but Brighton’s trip to Liverpool presents a credible opportunity to take a selective gamble against them. Liverpool’s reputation for defensive problems should not automatically make this an easy fixture for Brighton: their defensive numbers are strong, even if their attacking data has been underwhelming.

Groß is the Brighton player to retain in the XI. His advanced positioning, share of set pieces and penalty potential give him multiple routes to returns, making him harder to bench even in a tougher away match. Estupiñán carries substantial attacking upside from left-back, but is more exposed to the risk of a Liverpool goal and a lost clean sheet, so he is the more sensible Brighton asset to leave out if a viable alternative exists.

Lewis Hall away to Crystal Palace is preferred to Estupiñán in this squad. Palace have just conceded five goals to Brighton in Gameweek 7, so Newcastle’s fixture remains appealing despite the team’s mixed form. Alexander Isak’s return and encouraging performances when fit also strengthen the case for backing Newcastle. Starting Estupiñán is not a mistake, particularly for managers without a stronger bench option, but replacing him with a player expected to outscore him by even one or two points is a worthwhile differential move in a highly owned FPL landscape.

The final decision may be dictated by squad fitness. Injuries elsewhere, including Morgan Gibbs-White and Erling Haaland concerns, can force Estupiñán back into the starting side. Absent those selection problems, the preferred call is to start Groß and Hall, with Estupiñán first substitute.
key_points: Start Pascal Groß against Liverpool because his positioning, set pieces and possible penalties preserve his return potential.
Bench Pervis Estupiñán if a credible alternative is available, as Liverpool’s defensive data is strong and Brighton may lose the clean sheet.
Lewis Hall is favoured away to Crystal Palace after Palace concede five goals to Brighton in Gameweek 7.
Liverpool’s attacking numbers are poor, so starting Estupiñán remains defensible despite the difficult fixture.
Alexander Isak’s return to fitness and form improves Newcastle’s appeal against Crystal Palace.

items.title: FPL GW8 Transfer Tips! | Buy, Sell, Keep, Avoid #fpl
items.headline: Buy Bryan Mbeumo as Savinho’s injury opens a clear Gameweek 8 transfer route
items.summary:
Bryan Mbeumo is the standout Gameweek 8 buy despite Manchester United’s poor overall form. FPL managers are selecting the player rather than the team, and United’s attacking play increasingly runs through Mbeumo. Only Erling Haaland and Ollie Watkins have recorded more shots and expected goals than the £7.8m midfielder so far, while his additional creative output strengthens his appeal as a relatively affordable premium attacker.

Savinho is the recommended sale after the Manchester City winger suffers an injury expected to keep him out for around eight weeks. His absence can create more opportunities for Jérémy Doku and Jack Grealish, with Phil Foden also capable of playing wide, but Savinho owners should not wait for a replacement within Pep Guardiola’s rotation-prone attack. Moving directly to Mbeumo offers a clearer route to regular minutes, talismanic involvement and immediate points potential.

Morgan Gibbs-White is a hold rather than a player to sell. The Nottingham Forest midfielder is close to featuring in Gameweek 7, suggesting he should be available for the Gameweek 8 meeting with Ipswich. That fixture is too favourable to abandon Forest’s main attacking figure: Gibbs-White takes penalties and has the central role needed to capitalise, so patience is preferred over an early transfer out.

Avoid Brighton defender Maxim De Cuyper for now. Away trips to Liverpool and Manchester City in the next two gameweeks make clean sheets unlikely, undermining the main source of his recent FPL returns. His attacking numbers—four shots across six gameweeks and 12 key passes—are respectable but not enough to offset those difficult fixtures on their own. Even existing owners may want to bench him, while prospective buyers can revisit the move from Gameweek 10 onwards.
key_points: Buy Bryan Mbeumo at £7.8m: he remains Manchester United’s leading attacking outlet and ranks behind only Erling Haaland and Ollie Watkins for shots and xG.
Sell Savinho after his reported eight-week injury absence, with Mbeumo the preferred replacement.
Manchester City’s wide positions may offer more minutes to Jérémy Doku and Jack Grealish, while Phil Foden can also move out wide, but rotation remains a risk.
Keep Morgan Gibbs-White if possible, as he is expected to be fit for Nottingham Forest’s favourable Gameweek 8 match against Ipswich.
Gibbs-White’s penalty duties and talismanic role make him worth holding through a potentially profitable fixture.
Avoid Maxim De Cuyper before away matches against Liverpool and Manchester City; his clean-sheet potential drops sharply.
Current De Cuyper owners can consider benching him for the next two gameweeks and reassessing a purchase around Gameweek 10.

items.title: "Why are you fielding 5 Defenders?" 🤷🏼‍♂️ | Tom Freeman's Gameweek 8 FPL Team Selection
items.headline: João Pedro arrives as Szoboszlai exit sets up a 4-4-2
items.summary:
The current five-defender selection is only temporary, forced by Everton’s difficult away fixture at Arsenal and a weakened midfield. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and Thierno Barry are benched for that match, while Dominik Szoboszlai also cannot be relied upon after a recurrence of an old injury that Liverpool intend to manage carefully.

João Pedro has already replaced Yoane Wissa immediately after the previous deadline. The move captures a price rise for João Pedro and a price fall for Wissa, and had been planned a week earlier. It was delayed because there was already enough exposure to the Everton-Chelsea match, making another attacker from that fixture an unnecessary extra risk.

With four free transfers still available and £0.5m in the bank, the priority is to sell Szoboszlai. His replacement is expected to come straight into the starting XI, allowing a switch from five at the back to a 4-4-2. The remaining decision is which defender makes way: Neco Williams and Hall are the two candidates, with the final call dependent on the preferred fixture and defensive upside.
key_points: João Pedro replaces Yoane Wissa immediately after the deadline, benefiting from João Pedro’s price rise and Wissa’s fall.
Dominik Szoboszlai is set to be sold after an old injury recurs and requires careful management.
Everton’s trip to Arsenal makes Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and Thierno Barry bench options rather than starters.
Four free transfers and £0.5m in the bank give flexibility to bring in a starting midfielder for Szoboszlai.
The planned formation is 4-4-2 once Szoboszlai’s replacement arrives, rather than fielding five defenders.
Neco Williams or Hall is likely to be the defender dropped for the new midfielder.

items.title: 🚨 Maresca gives Haaland update ✅ FPL Gameweek 8 Preview 🔥
items.headline: Haaland remains the captaincy safety net as Chelsea alternatives fail to convince for Gameweek 8
items.summary:
Erling Haaland remains the default Gameweek 8 captain despite Manchester City’s trip to Aston Villa. He is rested in midweek European action and Maresca says he can start, so there is no reason to sell him unless the pre-match press conference brings fresh doubts. Aston Villa away is not an ideal fixture, but it is not difficult enough to demand a move away from Haaland; if in doubt, he keeps the armband. Chelsea’s home match against Spurs provides the strongest alternative, with Cole Palmer the preferred option over João Pedro because of penalties and midfielder scoring, but Palmer’s 0.34 expected goal involvement per 90 is a concern. Bukayo Saka against Everton and Bruno Fernandes against Bournemouth are viable differential captains, though both rely more on past pedigree than current returns.

Manchester City midfielders remain risky transfer punts. Phil Foden scores a Champions League hat-trick, but Doku and Injai are rested and look likelier to start against Villa, while Cherki also competes for the No. 10 role. There is no reliable route to guaranteed minutes among City’s attackers, so Foden, Doku and Injai are short-term gambles rather than clear buys. O’Riley misses the squad with a recurring back problem, while Vardyol also feels his back in the warm-up but is declared okay; owners can hold Vardyol if they can bench him against Villa, but neither defender is a buy. Liverpool’s Isak is rested in Europe and retains penalty appeal for now, but fitness history and the future return of Szoboszlai make him less compelling than his upside suggests. Barkley is an interesting differential but is behind Brennan Johnson, Gibbs-White and Rogers at his price.

A Gameweek 8 Free Hit leans into Arsenal’s home fixture against Everton, with Raya and Calafiori forming part of a defensive core alongside Konsa and Murillo. The attack includes Palmer, Rogers, João Pedro, Gibbs-White, Isak and Haaland, with Chelsea’s home game against Spurs supplying the main upside. Thiago of Brentford is the budget differential alternative to Isak. There is no urgent universal Free Hit target week, however: Gameweeks 17 to 19 offer potential opportunities, while Gameweek 19 could suit a one-week triple-up on Arsenal against Ipswich, Liverpool against Coventry and City against Spurs.

For a wildcard, the structure prioritises Raya, Calafiori and Saka from Arsenal, alongside a deep rotating defence featuring Murillo, de Cuyper, Castagne, Silva and van Hecke. The front line of João Pedro, Haaland and Calvert-Lewin is considered dependable, while Rogers, Mitoma and either Gibbs-White or Mbeumo provide midfield value. Brighton become a major target from Gameweek 10 due to their long favourable fixture run, but Kostas is best avoided until after Liverpool and Manchester City: seven returns in seven games is impressive, yet regular early substitutions and competition for Brighton slots make Calvert-Lewin preferable. Pascal Groß and de Cuyper should generally be started rather than forced out against Liverpool, while Tavernier is a clear hold—and still a possible buy—because of strong underlying numbers, penalties for now and a favourable run beginning with Leeds in Gameweek 9.
key_points: Captain Haaland against Aston Villa unless late City team news creates a genuine fitness concern; Palmer is the leading alternative against Spurs.
Foden’s hat-trick does not solve City’s rotation problem, with Doku, Injai and Cherki all competing for limited attacking places.
Hold Vardyol if he can be benched in Gameweek 8, but do not buy him or O’Riley while both have back-related uncertainty.
Chelsea attackers are the main Gameweek 8 Free Hit target, while a triple Arsenal defence or double Arsenal defence plus Saka is attractive against Everton.
Do not force a Free Hit now: Gameweeks 17-19, especially Gameweek 19, offer later opportunities if the chip remains unused.
Brighton assets become stronger transfer targets from Gameweek 10, but wait on Kostas until after Liverpool and Manchester City because his minutes are not secure.
Tavernier is a definite hold despite reduced recent minutes and a possible future loss of penalties; Bournemouth’s Gameweek 9-13 schedule is appealing.
For defenders at £5.0m or below, target Mee if buying for Gameweek 8, then consider van Hecke, Silva and Vuskovic according to the fixtures in which they need to start.

items.title: My transfer tips ahead of Gameweek 8 #fpl #fantasypremierleague #fpltips
items.headline: Semenyo injury forces Gameweek 8 sale as Calvert-Lewin leads budget-forward options
items.summary:
Semenyo is the clearest transfer out for Gameweek 8 after an eight-week injury lay-off that is expected to keep him unavailable until Gameweek 16. His absence may improve Doku’s chances of regular minutes, but Morgan Rogers, Minteh and Morgan Gibbs-White are preferred midfield replacements for only slightly more money. Inai, priced at £5.8m, offers a cheap route into Manchester City’s attack, although his minutes carry risk if Pep Guardiola moves Phil Foden wide.

Managers without Kyper are advised to wait until after the Liverpool and Manchester City fixtures before buying. At the back, Bobby Thomas is the standout ultra-budget defender: Coventry’s defence is unconvincing, but Thomas has defensive-contribution potential and a favourable fixture run. Pedro Neto is a less appealing midfield option because using a Chelsea slot on him could prevent moves for more valuable Chelsea assets, while Manzambi and Tavernier offer comparable or better value.

Alexander Isak remains an attractive forward in isolation, particularly with Sosai injured and penalties potentially in his hands. However, he is not worth restructuring a squad with two or more transfers to afford. Holding Whistler for another week is acceptable despite Newcastle’s poor form, as Crystal Palace are also struggling. For managers needing a cheap striker immediately, Dominic Calvert-Lewin is the leading choice thanks to secure minutes and penalty duties, with Evanilson and Nicolas Jackson viable lower-owned alternatives. Gonzalo Garcia and Josh King should be held for the Coventry fixture, which offers promise for Fulham.
key_points: Sell Semenyo in Gameweek 8, with his injury expected to rule him out until around Gameweek 16.
Rogers, Minteh and Gibbs-White are preferred midfield replacements over Doku, whose minutes remain uncertain.
Inai costs £5.8m and offers Manchester City attacking exposure, but Foden playing wide remains a rotation threat.
Wait to buy Kyper until after the Liverpool and Manchester City matches if you have managed without him so far.
Bobby Thomas is the preferred cheap defender because of his defensive-contribution appeal and favourable fixtures.
Do not take multiple transfers or major squad surgery to reach Isak, despite his possible penalty upside.
Calvert-Lewin is the preferred budget forward due to reliable starts and penalties; Evanilson and Jackson are lower-owned alternatives.
Hold Gonzalo Garcia and Josh King for the Coventry game rather than selling immediately.

items.title: PREMIUM PLAYERS WORTH THE MONEY? 🤔 | FPL EXPERT GW8 TEAM REVEAL ✅ | FPL Tips 26/27
items.headline: João Pedro arrives as Tom Freeman bins Szoboszlai and weighs captaincy over Haaland
items.summary:
Tom Freeman heads into Gameweek 8 with four free transfers after bringing in João Pedro for Wissa immediately after Gameweek 7. The move exploits a price rise for Pedro and a drop for Wissa, while adding Brighton’s most reliable attacking asset despite a home match against Tottenham. Freeman had considered Brighton additions earlier but waited through tougher fixtures; their scoring form now makes their attackers difficult to ignore, even against Liverpool and Manchester City. Brighton have been among Europe’s most potent attacks, so their players retain upside regardless of opponent.

Szoboszlai is Freeman’s clear next sale after suffering a recurrence of an old injury, with a mid-priced midfielder the likely replacement. Schär is currently top of the shortlist because of Brentford’s upcoming games against Hull and Forest, although his reduced minutes on return from a shoulder injury are a concern. Morgan Rogers is also considered, but Manchester City is not viewed as the ideal entry fixture, even if Aston Villa are expected to score at Villa Park. Freeman plans to move to a 4-4-2, probably benching either Hall or Williams; Hall is marginally preferred despite Newcastle’s poor form, as Ipswich are scoring regularly and Crystal Palace look vulnerable.

Further Everton exits are possible, with Barry and Dewsbury-Hall both expendable because Freeman does not want to carry a double Everton attack in a low-scoring side. Calvert-Lewin is a possible forward replacement, while Dewsbury-Hall could become Tavernier or Rogers. However, Freeman sees Gameweek 8 as a difficult week to force multiple moves: many targets have drawbacks, clean-sheet prospects are limited and he would rather preserve flexibility for Gameweek 9 and beyond.

Captaincy is between Haaland away to Aston Villa and Chelsea’s João Pedro at home to Tottenham, with Palmer also under consideration. Freeman leans towards Pedro because he offers several routes to points, including penalties, shots and possible assists, although Tottenham’s recent defensive displays temper expectations. Haaland remains a safe default and is expected to get chances against a Villa defence carrying injuries, but Freeman doubts City will score heavily. The broader strategy is to avoid overpaying for underperforming premiums: Haaland is essential, Isak becomes attractive when Liverpool’s fixtures improve from Gameweek 10, and Saka retains some appeal on underlying numbers, but Palmer, Gabriel and Bruno Fernandes currently fail to justify their prices.
key_points: João Pedro replaces Wissa before Gameweek 8, giving Freeman Brighton attacking coverage and retaining four free transfers.
Szoboszlai is set to leave after an injury recurrence, with Schär the leading midfield replacement target.
Freeman plans a 4-4-2 and is likely to bench Williams rather than Hall, although Ipswich’s attacking form makes the call close.
Barry and Dewsbury-Hall are possible sales because double Everton attack offers limited upside; Calvert-Lewin, Tavernier and Rogers are alternatives.
Haaland and João Pedro are the leading captaincy choices, with Freeman leaning toward Pedro at home to Tottenham but viewing Haaland as the safer high-owned pick.
Haaland is the only fully convincing premium now; Isak is earmarked as a potential addition from Gameweek 10 when Liverpool’s schedule improves.
Palmer, Gabriel and Bruno Fernandes are viewed as overpriced on current output, while Saka’s altered, more goal-focused role has reduced his assist potential.
